key_insight: EvoPINN turns PINN design into an execution-grounded search problem, using an LLM agent to iteratively discover scientifically valid PDE-solving algorithms and architectures.
engineering_relevance: For scientific and solid-mechanics-style PDE workflows, this suggests a path to automate model and training-design choices while respecting numerical constraints and improving solution accuracy.
method: Decouple neural representations from training programs in a modular search space.
Use an LLM agent to propose memory-conditioned code modifications iteratively.
Filter candidates with structural verification and budget-matched PDE evaluation.
evidence_signal: Across oscillatory, elliptic, dissipative, and nonlinear transport PDEs, the method reportedly reduces relative L2 error and the discovered SLRC-PINN remains strong under parameter-matched comparisons.
watch_item: The approach still depends on reliable verification, fair budget matching, and stable execution of generated programs, which may limit practicality on harder or more expensive PDE setups.
paper_title: EvoPINN: Agentic Discovery of Executable Algorithms for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
